To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
realized strategies and administrative systems interact with each other and with performance in a three-way interaction.

the performance implications of realized marketing strategy depend on the alignment of the dynamic administrative system parameters of interdepartmental connected-ness and control mechanisms with realized strategy type.
realized strategies are not always implemented as planned.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance implications of realized strategies and the misalignments of administrative systems with these strategies.
the performance implications of misalignments between realized marketing strategies, the administrative systems designed to support them, and the performance of the firms.
the performance implications of realized marketing strategies and their (mis)alignment with administrative systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

firms should design administrative systems that support the implementation of their realized strategies, and that the effectiveness of these systems depends on the type of realized strategy and the degree of (mis)alignment between the strategy and its supporting system.
the more centralized and formalized the system, the more effective the strategy implementation.
firms with realized differentiation strategies should centralize, formalize, and specialize the marketing department, and they should have a high level of connectedness and formal control mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

realized strategies are not only important for firm performance but also the alignment (or misalignment) between realized strategies and the administrative system is also important for firm performance.
the performance implications of misalignments between realized strategies and the administrative system are contingent upon the nature of the marketing strategy.
firms need to design administrative systems that can adapt to the dynamic business environment and that can support the implementation of realized strategies in order to achieve superior performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of the administrative system should reflect the realized marketing strategy and not the originally intended strategy.
firms need to align realized strategies with the dynamic parameters of their administrative system to achieve superior performance.
the performance implications of realized strategy misalignments are not always as straightforward as the performance implications of intended strategy misalignments.
